name: Kofta bil Tahiniyyeh (Kofta Baked in a Lemony-Tahini Sauce)

ingredients.name: fresh parsley, plus more for serving

instructions.primary_message: Finely chop the yellow onion. Pick the parsley leaves from the stems and finely chop them. Juice the lemons. Grate or finely mince the garlic.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 medium yellow onion
¾ cup fresh parsley, plus more for serving
4 lemons
1 medium clove garlic

instructions.primary_message: For the Kofta: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 425°F.

In a large bowl, combine beef and/or lamb, onion, parsley, cinnamon, cardamom, allspice, black pepper, and salt. Using clean hands, mix until thoroughly combined. Divide mixture into about 25 approximately equal portions and shape each portion into an oval patty about 2 3/4 to 3 inches long and 1 inch thick (they do not need to be exact).

In a 9- by 13-inch baking dish, arrange kofta in a flat, even layer, squeezing them close together as needed. Shingle potato slices over kofta, using about 5 slices per row, and distribute tomato slices (if using) evenly across baking dish. Nestle chile pepper, if using, in the center of baking dish. Cover baking dish tightly with aluminum foil and bake until potatoes are tender but not falling apart when pierced with a paring knife, 45 to 50 minutes.

For the Tahini Sauce: Meanwhile, in a medium bowl, whisk tahini, lemon juice, yogurt (if using), garlic, and salt until mixture is smooth and thickens. Gradually whisk in water until smooth and pourable.

To Finish Kofta: Once potatoes are tender, remove baking dish from oven and discard foil. Pour tahini sauce evenly over kofta, potatoes, and tomatoes. Return to oven and bake, uncovered, until sauce is bubbling and slightly thickened but still loose enough to pool around the kofta and vegetables, and the surface is lightly browned in some spots, 10 to 15 minutes (be careful not to overbake or tahini sauce will break). Sprinkle with parsley and serve with pita or vermicelli rice.

description: This one-dish kofta is an easy Palestinian casserole of spiced ground beef or lamb and tender potatoes baked in a rich, lemony tahini sauce.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 medium tomatoes (10 ounces; 283 g total), sliced into 1/2-inch-thick rounds (optional); 1 green chile pepper such as jalapeño (optional); 2 tablespoons plain whole milk yogurt, optional (see notes)

Optional substitutions: ground beef → ground lamb; Pita bread → vermicelli rice

Notes: If using a mixture of lamb and beef, use 95% lean ground beef, since the lamb contributes enough fat to keep the kofta juicy and tender. If using all beef, use 85% lean ground beef so the kofta has enough fat to stay moist during cooking.
Adding yogurt to the tahini sauce makes it creamier. For a more traditional flavor and texture, don’t substitute Greek-style strained yogurt for plain yogurt.

Make-ahead and storage: Kofta can be made and shaped into patties up to 4 days in advance.
It’s best not to make the tahini sauce in advance, as it may thicken too much as it sits in the refrigerator.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat gently in the oven, stovetop, or microwave, adding a splash of water to loosen sauce as needed.
author: Laila Ibrahim
